spec.question: Clarify `SessionCSRF` behavior at expiry boundaries and when expiration is disabled. Use the same secret `b"secret"` and session mapping `{"csrf": "fixed-session"}` throughout, with untranslated error messages. At a controlled issue time of 2030-01-02 03:04:05, generate token A using Meta with no `csrf_time_limit` attribute, and token B using Meta with `csrf_time_limit=None`. Report each token's serialized expiry prefix before `##`. Also report the validation outcome for these seven cases: A under the default time limit at 03:34:05 that day (`a_at_boundary`); A under the default limit at 03:34:06 (`a_after_boundary`); B with expiration disabled on 2031-01-02 (`b_disabled_later`); B under the default limit at the issue time (`b_with_default_limit`); A with expiration disabled on 2031-01-02 (`a_disabled_later`); A with its first digest character changed to a different hexadecimal character, under the default limit at 03:34:06 (`tampered_expired_a`); and an empty submitted token under the default limit (`empty_token`). Assume each implementation has completed setup and token generation before validation. Return a JSON object with `expires_a`, `expires_b`, and `outcomes`; map each case name in `outcomes` to null for success or the exact validation error message.
